comments_text: Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is unique and shows only very low similarity (81.25%) to Tur1B R: 25%, P: 31%. GRAVY: -1.11; mol wt: 4032.861; mol formula: C193H299N59O36; mol ex coeff: 11100. Activity: active against E. coli ATCC 25922 (MIC 6 uM), E. faecium ATCC 19434 (MIC 16 uM), S. aureus ATCC 25923 (MIC 32 uM), K. pneumoniae ATCC 700603 (MIC 32 uM), A. baumannii ATCC 19606 (MIC 2 uM), P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 (MIC 32 uM), E. agglomerans clinical isolate (MIC 8 uM), S. maltophilia ATCC 13637 (MIC 2 uM), C. albicans ATCC 90029 (MIC 4 uM), MOA:bacteria: E. coli BW25113 (MIC 8 uM), E. coli BW25113 delta SbmA (MIC 2 uM). This transporter may not be the primary mechanism for peptide action. The peptide permeated bacterial membranes and also inhibited protein synthesis in an in vitro assay. Antimicrobial robustness: media had an effect since the peptide showed higher activity in 20% diluted MHB.

comments_text: Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is unique and shows only very low similarity (57.14%) to buCATHL4D R: 16%, P: 32%, F: 21%, W: 11%. GRAVY: -0.594; mol wt: 2399.837; mol formula: C122H165N31O21; mol ex coeff: 11100. Activity: active against E. coli ATCC 25922 (MIC 16 uM), E-faecium ATCC 19434 (MIC >64 uM), S. aureus ATCC 25923 (MIC 16 uM), K-pneumoniae ATCC 700603 (MIC >64 uM), A. baumannii ATCC 19606 (MIC 16 uM), P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 (MIC 64 uM), E. agglomerans clinical isolate (MIC 64 uM), S. maltophilia ATCC 13637 (MIC 24 uM), C. albicans ATCC 90029 (MIC 32 uM), MOA:bacteria: E. coli BW25113 (MIC 24 uM), E. coli BW25113 delta SbmA (MIC 16 uM). This transporter may not be the primary mechanism for peptide action. The peptide permeated bacterial membranes and also inhibited protein synthesis in an in vitro assay. Antimicrobial robustness: media had an effect since the peptide showed higher activity in 20% diluted MHB. Discovery: Neo1 is a sequence truncated peptide due to a premature stop codon. This led to weaker activity (MIC 16 uM or greater) compared to other peptides reported in the same article.
